titulo: Living in Spain or Latin America: banks, mobile phones and renting: Review and practice of lesson 58

aula.titulo: Living in Spain or Latin America: banks, mobile phones and renting
aula.objetivo: Ask for information and handle everyday paperwork in Spanish: open and use a bank account, sign up for and complain about a mobile or internet service, and view and negotiate a rental, knowing what changes between Spain and Latin America.

itens.enunciado: You're looking for a plan and don't know if one exists. Which sentence do you use?
opcoes: Busco una tarifa que incluya muchos datos.
Busco una tarifa que incluye muchos datos.
Busco una tarifa que incluir muchos datos.
itens.gabarito: Busco una tarifa que incluya muchos datos.
itens.explicacao: An indefinite antecedent takes the subjunctive in the relative clause.

itens.enunciado: In Spain, what does «ingresar dinero» mean?
itens.explicacao: «Ingresar» is to deposit; going into a place is «entrar».

itens.enunciado: Which word is used for "cell phone" in Latin America?

itens.enunciado: Quisiera ___ dinero. (sacar)

itens.enunciado: Me gustaría saber si ___ cobertura en mi zona. (haber)
itens.explicacao: After «saber si», indicative: «hay».

itens.enunciado: Busco un piso que ___ terraza. (tener)

itens.enunciado: What does «la fianza» mean in a rental contract?

blocos.enunciado: Choose one of the three tasks (bank, phone or rental) and say out loud, in 6 sentences, what you'd ask and what you'd check afterwards in current sources.
Say three sentences in Spanish for the bank, three for the phone provider and three for the landlord. Remember: always check the current rules.
